newsitem.title: HONG KONG: People's choice won't enter HK leadership race.
newsitem.headline: People's choice won't enter HK leadership race.

text.p: Hong Kong Chief Secretary Anson Chan, the people's choice for the territory's first chief executive, ended months of speculation on Saturday and announced that she would not be joining the race for the top post.

"After careful consideration of all the relevant factors governing the selection process and having consulted my senior colleagues within the civil service, I have decided not to put my name forward as a candidate for the chief executive post," the head of the colony's civil service said.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, 1997, at which point British Governor Chris Patten will be replaced by a chief executive appointed by a 400-member selection board.
Chan has consistently topped polls as the most preferred choice to lead the territory after the handover, although she had declined to state her intentions until now.

Popularity will count for little since the selection board will by chosen by a China-appointed Preparatory Committee, however. The committee is responsible for overseeing Hong Kong's transfer of sovereignty.
Chief Justice Sir Ti Liang Yang ranks second in the popularity stakes ahead of shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa, businessman Peter Woo and former Appeal Court judge Simon Li.
